llm.summary: The skill's declared metadata (no requirements / no credentials) doesn't match its runtime instructions and scripts, and the docs/shell instructions encourage the agent to store API keys in the user's filesystem without clear user consent.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (publish Sites and store Drive files) matches the two included scripts (publish.sh and drive.sh). However the registry metadata claims no required binaries or env vars, while SKILL.md and the scripts require curl, file, jq and optionally HERENOW_API_KEY / HERENOW_DRIVE_TOKEN and ~/.herenow/credentials — an incoherence between declared metadata and actual needs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read docs at https://here.now/docs and to save API keys to ~/.herenow/credentials (and explicitly says not to ask the user to run it manually), which encourages the agent to write secrets to disk. The scripts read local files and will upload arbitrary files to the service (which is the stated purpose) but the instruction to persist API keys without explicit user-run action expands agent privileges and should be confirmed with the user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only), so nothing is downloaded or written by an installer. The skill bundles two shell scripts; they rely on system tools (curl, jq, file) or a bundled jq if present. No remote arbitrary downloads are performed by an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The scripts legitimately use an account API key and drive tokens for their functionality, but the registry lists no primary credential and no required env vars while SKILL.md marks HERENOW_API_KEY and HERENOW_DRIVE_TOKEN as optional. The guidance to persist credentials in ~/.herenow without explicit user confirmation increases risk of secrets being written/used by the agent. The skill will also read .herenow/state.json and credentials files — appropriate for function but sensitive in practice.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and agent invocation is normal. The skill reads and writes under ~/.herenow (credential/state files) which is expected for a CLI that stores keys/state. The actionable concern is the textual instruction that agents should save API keys themselves (not ask the user), which raises the chance of silent persistence of credentials if the agent follows it.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the publish/drive features it advertises, but there are mismatches and a few risky instructions you should evaluate before installing:

- Metadata mismatch: the skill registry claims no required binaries or credentials, but the scripts and SKILL.md require curl, file, jq and optional HERENOW_API_KEY / HERENOW_DRIVE_TOKEN and use ~/.herenow/credentials. Ask the publisher to correct the metadata or provide the source repo.
- Credentials handling: SKILL.md tells the agent to persist API keys to ~/.herenow/credentials and says not to ask the user to run the command manually — this effectively encourages the agent to write secrets to your filesystem. Only allow this if you trust the skill and its service; prefer manual key entry or a review step before writing credentials.
- Network & privacy: the scripts upload arbitrary local files to the here.now service. Ensure you only publish intended content and that the service/domain (here.now) is legitimate/trustworthy. Verify https://here.now/docs and the API endpoints resolve to a domain you trust.
- Operational checks: confirm there is no bundled binary missing (SKILL_DIR/bin/jq was referenced but not included in the manifest) and that jq/curl/file are available in your environment.

If you are uncomfortable with automatic credential persistence or uploading files programmatically, do not grant the agent permission to run these scripts autonomously; instead use manual workflows or require explicit user confirmation before any credential writes or uploads.
